description.comment: Lord Derby's scaly-tailed squirrel (Anomalurus derbianus) is an anomalurid rodent native to Africa, living in tropical and subtropical rainforests in western and central Africa (from Wikipedia entry). This sample of a female individual found in the Democratic Republic of Congo was collected by W.T. Stanley and coordinated by Adam Ferguson of the Field Natural Museum of History in Chicago and Paul Hime of Washington University in Saint Louis to generate a high-quality reference genome for the Vertebrate Genomes Project (VGP). Sequencing and genome assembly were conducted at the Vertebrate Genome Lab (VGL) at the Rockefeller University, led by Erich D. Jarvis, Giulio Formenti, and Jennifer Balacco. We note that the mitogenome generated for this individual showed 89.39% similarity with an Anomalurus pelii mitogenome (NC_038172.1) vs. 88.83% with an Anomalurus derbianus mitogenome (NC_038173.1) on BLAST, and not a higher identity to any other species in GenBank at the time of submisson. We are submitting the assembly under the A. derbianus species name, given that was the original vouchered specimen indentification.

assembly_info.comments: Curator note: There is no known karyotype for this species. 27 pairs of chromosomes were identified in the Hi-C map (2n=54). Chromosome X was identified by synteny to Neotoma floridana smalli (GCA_050000055.1). In chromosome 3 of both haplotypes there is a small fragment of duplicate Hi-C signal at 120.4Mbp, but no gaps at this location. In haplotype 1, chromosome 15 has duplicate signal at 2.3-2.9Mbp, but no gaps at this location, indicating that these ar real duplications
